subject: Clarifying erase process and chain-of-custody artifacts for tenant deactivation
messages:
From: Tom Byrne <t.byrne@acme-corp.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Security <security@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T09:12:00Z
Subject: Chain-of-custody proof for tenant erasure - initial ask

Hi Jasmine,

We're starting the decommission for a small tenant and the external auditors asked for a clear chain-of-custody and artifact set that proves complete erasure. Specifically they're asking for:
- Step-by-step deletion workflow (who/what/when) for tenant data across storage tiers
- Examples of deletion logs that link tenant IDs to object-level erasures
- Evidence that any backups or snapshots are accounted for or expired
- Any cryptographic / HSM key rotation evidence used to render data unrecoverable (if applicable)

Can you point me to where we can get a concise packet (PDF or CSV examples) we can hand to auditors? Also whether you have a standard attestation wording for SOC 2/ISO reviews would be helpful.

Thanks,
Tom Byrne
Head of Security Ops
Acme Corp

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Tom Byrne <t.byrne@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Chain-of-custody proof for tenant erasure - initial ask

Tom —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick note on scope: we can produce an auditor-friendly packet that maps to SOC 2/ISO expectations (control objectives around retention, deletion, and evidence). I attached a high-level flowchart and a small sample deletion log snippet to illustrate the format.

What we'll include in the packet:
- Deletion workflow diagram (logical steps + owner per step) — attached as PDF
- Sample deletion log CSV with pseudonymized tenant IDs and timestamps — attached
- Backup/snapshot retention mapping and expiration proof (summary doc we can add)
- Key-rotation statement (if the tenant used envelope encryption) 
- Suggested attestation language that your auditors can accept (SOC 2/ISO phrasing)

Next steps for us: Vivek will pull a redacted end-to-end export of the deletion event chain (object deletes, cache invalidation, snapshot expiry records). Laura will provide the standard attestation language and link it back to the SOC 2 CC3/ISO 27001 clause references.

Would you like the packet as a single ZIP with a cover letter, or separate artifacts so you can drop individual files into your evidence repository?

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redo Inference (Redwood)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Tom Byrne <t.byrne@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T08:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Chain-of-custody proof for tenant erasure - initial ask

Tom / Jasmine —

I pulled the tech-side artifacts you asked about. Summary here (I can export the full redacted CSVs this week):

1) Deletion event chain (what we can provide):
   - API call records (tenant-id, request-id, user/service principal, timestamp, fields deleted) from our audit pipeline
   - Storage object delete entries from object store (object path, hash, delete-marker timestamp)
   - KV cache invalidation logs (cache-key, TTL, invalidation timestamp)
   - Snapshot retention manifest showing snapshot IDs and expiry timestamps; snapshots are purged by a scheduled job and we emit a purge event

2) Cross-checks / linking keys:
   - request-id and object-hash are present in both API and storage logs so you can link the call to the object erasure
   - we include tenant namespace in every record (namespaced prefix) so auditors can map to tenant scope without exposing PII

3) Backups & Escrow:
   - Hosted accounts: we retain encrypted backups for 30 days before automatic purge; manifest includes cryptographic hashes and rotation metadata.
   - Dedicated/Private: backup behaviour depends on customer config; we'll include a config summary for your tenant showing retention windows

4) Key handling:
   - If customer-managed keys (BYOK) were used, the attestation references customer KMS policy and the fact that a key destruction or rotation renders the backup inaccessible — we'll include a redacted KMS key rotation log (timestamp + key-id reference).

I'll prepare three files: full redacted deletion-event CSV, storage-delete manifest, and snapshot-expiry-manifest. ETA: EOD Tuesday (2026-11-09).

-Vivek
Principal Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Tom Byrne <t.byrne@acme-corp.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T12:14:00Z
Subject: Re: Chain-of-custody proof for tenant erasure - initial ask

Tom —

Attached is the recommended attestation language we use for SOC 2 and ISO evidence bundles. A short excerpt below you can copy into your audit packet: 

"Redwood Inference attests that, for the tenant identified by the provided tenant namespace, deletion requests initiated via the documented API or Console result in recorded deletion events across API, storage, cache, and snapshot manifests. Backups are subject to defined retention policies, and for hosted accounts retained no longer than the documented windows. Where BYOK is employed, key rotation or customer key retirement is included as part of the irrecoverability proof. Redwood will provide redacted event logs and manifests as evidence subject to NDA and redaction rules."

Mapping to controls: SOC 2 CC6 (Logical access to data), CC7 (Change management) and ISO 27001 A.12.3 (backup) and A.8.3 (removal). We'll add control references in the final cover letter.

Suggested deliverable set for auditors:
- Cover letter + attestation (PDF)
- Redacted deletion events CSV (CSV)
- Storage delete manifest (CSV)
- Snapshot expiry manifest (CSV)
- Flowchart of the erase process (PDF)
- Redacted KMS rotation log (if BYOK) (CSV)

I can sign off on the attestation PDF once Vivek's artifacts are attached.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Manager, Compliance & Controls
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Byrne <t.byrne@acme-corp.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T17:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Chain-of-custody proof for tenant erasure - initial ask

Thanks — that looks perfect.

We prefer a single ZIP (cover letter + artifacts). Can you include a very small sample deletion log that maps to the manifest schema so our auditor can verify linking (pseudonymized tenant IDs are fine). If you can deliver by EOD Tuesday that will align with our audit window.

Also happy to jump on a 30-minute call tomorrow morning to walk auditors through the docs — propose 09:30 PT?

Tom Byrne
Head of Security Ops
Acme Corp
